news_drafts.headline: Newport's 2024-25 accounts certified with qualified opinion; bus company faces going-concern uncertainty
news_drafts.lead:
Newport City Council's external auditor certified its 2024-25 financial statements with a qualified opinion in August 2026, meaning it could not fully sign off the accounts. The auditor could not obtain sufficient evidence on the carrying amounts of Newport Transport Limited, the council's bus company, within the group accounts. The 2025-26 opinion has been delayed while that assurance is awaited, according to the Audit of Financial Statements Report 2025/26 before the Governance and Audit Committee on 26 November.

The same report says the company was loss-making in 2024-25 and 2025-26. In the auditor's words, this "indicate[s] the existence of a material uncertainty which may cast doubt on NTL's ability to continue as a going concern." The report states that the company's continued going concern status depends on returning to profitable trading.

The report records a sale and leaseback of the company's bus depot in October 2026, described as a cash injection. It also reports cost cutting and extended supplier payment terms as improvements in 2026-27.

news_drafts.headline: Newport forecasts £0.746m overspend for 2026/27 after contingency, with services £4.745m over
news_drafts.lead:
Newport City Council's September revenue monitoring report, going to Cabinet on 11 November, forecasts a net overspend of £0.746m for 2026/27, against a net revenue budget of £462.8m. That figure takes the contingency budget into account. Service areas, excluding schools, are forecast to overspend by £4.745m. The paper describes this as substantially offset by temporary underspends in non-service areas, including £1.636m on general contingency and £2.073m on capital financing.

Two services account for much of the service overspend. Housing Services is forecast to overspend by £2.992m. Temporary accommodation payments to landlords and hotels are forecast £1.1m over budget and income about £1.0m below budget, and alarm and security provision is £953k over. Planned mitigation of £342k is not being delivered, and the paper says this will carry into 2027/28. Children's residential placements are forecast to overspend by £2.170m. The paper attributes this to delays in new in-house capacity: 29 in-house placements across 11 properties are operating against 38 planned across 12. Nineteen children remain in out-of-area placements against a budget assumption of 11. Health and education contributions of £720k are expected to offset part of the cost.

Schools are forecast separately to overspend their revenue funding by £0.606m, met from school reserves. Balances are forecast to fall from £13.054m brought forward to £12.488m by March 2027. Forty-nine of 55 schools forecast an in-year overspend, two primary schools forecast a deficit, and about 59% of the forecast overspend funds recurring spending. The paper notes a Welsh Government additional learning needs grant of approximately £2.5m may ease pressures.

findings.headline: Children's Services net cost in the Comprehensive Income and Expenditure Statement was £37,111k in 2025/26, up from £32,543k in 2024/25.
findings.detail: The paper identifies Homelessness services and Children's Services as experiencing the most acute demand pressures in 2025/26. The Adult Services net cost in the same statement was £81,816k, up from £71,984k.
findings.matters: Rising net cost in demand-led social care services is a pressure other councils are tracking, and the scale of the increase is a direct comparison point.

findings.headline: Net assets rose by £102.7m to £572m at 31 March 2026, from £469.3m a year earlier.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the increase in the balance sheet to the movement between the two year-end positions. Usable reserves are separately reported as £120.8m.
findings.matters: A large rise in net assets, driven partly by asset revaluation, changes the balance sheet ratios lenders use to assess a council's position.
findings.quote: an increase of £102.7m in value between 2024/25 (net assets of £469.3m) and 2025/26 (net assets of £572m)

findings.headline: Auditor General for Wales gives an opinion that the 2025/26 financial statements give a true and fair view, with no material uncertainties on going concern.
findings.detail: The opinion covers both Newport City Council and the Group. The auditor reports no material uncertainties relating to going concern for at least 12 months from authorisation, and the date of the auditor's certificate is shown as TBC.
findings.matters: An unmodified opinion with no going concern uncertainty is the baseline a lender or finance director checks before relying on the accounts, and the audit completion date is still open in this paper.
findings.quote: In my opinion, in all material respects, the financial statements:

findings.headline: Auditor draws attention to Newport Transport Limited's current financial position and its assessment of future financial sustainability, without modifying the opinion.
findings.detail: The emphasis of matter is on the Group financial statements, where Newport Transport Limited is a wholly owned subsidiary and a material component of the Group. The auditor states that the opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.
findings.matters: An auditor emphasis of matter on a council-owned bus company's financial sustainability is the type of group-level risk a lender or finance director at another council would want to check.
findings.quote: I draw attention to page 115 within the Group financial statements which sets out the current fi nancial position of Newport Transport Limited

findings.headline: The Local Authority Trading Company arrangement for property services began on 1 January 2026, with the creation of the arrangement completed on time.
findings.detail: The paper says Cyson Cymru now provides property management, design, building maintenance, premises management and cleaning. As a wholly owned company it is included within the Group Statement of Accounts.
findings.matters: Moving property services into a wholly owned trading company changes the council's group structure and reporting, which other councils considering similar arrangements will want to see.
findings.quote: the creation of the Local Authority Trading Company (LATCO) arrangement to the deliver property services from 1st January 2026 was completed on time.
